milestones.title: Sprint 1 - Data foundation
milestones.description: Goal: the 2023-2025 HMDA files land in Delta, are typed, quality-checked and audited for leakage, and the model population exists with an out-of-time split.

milestones.title: Sprint 2 - Model
milestones.description: Goal: a calibrated TensorFlow model that beats the baselines on the 2025 hold-out, with a fair-lending audit, reason codes and a model card.

milestones.title: Sprint 3 - Serving and monitoring
milestones.description: Goal: real-time decisions through TF Serving and an authenticated API, decision events through Pub/Sub into BigQuery, drift and fairness monitoring with alerts, all from one command.

milestones.title: Sprint 4 - Cloud and release
milestones.description: Goal: Terraform for GCP and a Databricks Asset Bundle that validate in CI, a load test, and a README a hiring manager can read in two minutes.

milestones.title: Sprint 5 - Less discriminatory alternative
milestones.description: Goal: a joint search for a less discriminatory alternative to model v1, chosen on 2024 and scored once on 2025, with the result in the model card whether or not it passes.

milestones.title: Backlog
milestones.description: Not scheduled: work that needs an account or a later sprint.

issues.title: Repository scaffold, CI skeleton and dev environment
issues.body:
As a contributor, I want one command to set up the environment and a CI pipeline that lints and tests every push, so that broken code never reaches main.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] `uv sync` installs pinned dependencies (lock file committed)
- [ ] ruff, mypy and pytest run in CI on every push and pull request
- [ ] gitleaks runs before every push and in CI

issues.title: Download HMDA snapshots reproducibly
issues.body:
As a data engineer, I want a script that downloads the 2023-2025 national HMDA snapshot files with retries and a size check, so that anyone can rebuild the raw layer.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] `scripts/download_hmda.sh` resumes partial downloads and verifies the zip
- [ ] bats tests cover success, retry and corrupt-file paths
- [ ] shellcheck clean

issues.title: Bronze: land raw LAR files in Delta
issues.body:
As a data engineer, I want the raw CSVs stored unchanged in a Delta table partitioned by year, with file lineage, so that every later step is replayable.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] all columns kept as strings, plus `_source_file` and `_ingested_at`
- [ ] re-running a year replaces that partition only (idempotent)
- [ ] row counts recorded per file

issues.title: Silver: typed, decoded application records
issues.body:
As an analyst, I want typed columns with HMDA codes decoded (DTI bins, Exempt/NA sentinels, income in dollars), so that downstream code never parses strings.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] one documented contract (`schema.py`) shared by Spark and the API
- [ ] unit tests for every parser on real HMDA values

issues.title: Data quality checks with critical and warning severities
issues.body:
As a data owner, I want declarative quality checks that fail the pipeline on critical errors and report warnings, so that a bad file never trains a model.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] checks for allowed values, ranges, completeness, reconciliation bronze vs silver
- [ ] JSON report committed for the real run

issues.title: Leakage audit and model population with an out-of-time split
issues.body:
As a model risk reviewer, I want every candidate feature screened for post-decision leakage and the data split by year (train 2023, validate 2024, test 2025), so that the hold-out result is honest.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] availability gap and univariate AUC per field, flagged fields excluded
- [ ] protected attributes and tract demographics kept for audit only, never as features
- [ ] a test fails if a flagged field enters the feature list

issues.title: Benchmark the Spark pipeline on the full national files
issues.body:
As an engineer, I want measured stage timings and a core-scaling curve, so that capacity claims come from a run.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] `reports/spark-bench.json` with hardware, rows, seconds per stage
- [ ] silver stage timed at 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 cores

issues.title: Baselines: logistic regression and XGBoost
issues.body:
As a model reviewer, I want simple baselines on the same split and features, so that the neural model has to earn its place.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] AUC, KS, Brier, ECE on 2024 and 2025 for each baseline

issues.title: TensorFlow model with in-graph preprocessing
issues.body:
As an ML engineer, I want a Keras model whose preprocessing lives inside the SavedModel, so that training and serving cannot skew.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] raw typed inputs in, calibrated probability out
- [ ] `explain` signature returns integrated-gradient attributions per feature
- [ ] test: attributions sum to the logit difference from the baseline

issues.title: Out-of-time evaluation and calibration
issues.body:
As a credit risk lead, I want discrimination, calibration and stability measured on the untouched 2025 year, so that I know how the model ages.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] AUC with bootstrap CI, KS, Brier, ECE before and after Platt scaling
- [ ] PSI of every input between 2023 and 2025
- [ ] `reports/model-metrics.json` committed

issues.title: Fair-lending audit and model card
issues.body:
As a compliance officer, I want adverse impact ratios by race, ethnicity, sex and age compared with the lenders' own decisions, so that the model is not adopted if it widens disparities.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] AIR and per-group AUC at the operating threshold
- [ ] generated MODEL-CARD.md with data, metrics, limits and fairness

issues.title: Batch scoring in Spark
issues.body:
As an operations analyst, I want a Spark job that scores a whole year with the exported model, so that portfolio reviews do not go through the online API.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] mapInPandas with one model load per worker
- [ ] rows per second measured on the 2025 year

issues.title: Real-time decision API in front of TF Serving
issues.body:
As a loan officer system, I want a validated, authenticated endpoint that returns a decision, probability and adverse-action reasons, so that every referral can be explained.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] API keys, request validation, rate limit, health and readiness
- [ ] reasons come from the model's explain signature

issues.title: Decision events through Pub/Sub into BigQuery
issues.body:
As a model monitor, I want every decision published as an event and stored in BigQuery, so that drift and fairness can be measured on live traffic.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] works against the Pub/Sub and BigQuery emulators locally
- [ ] failed messages go to a dead-letter topic

issues.title: Integration tests with Testcontainers
issues.body:
As a contributor, I want the API, TF Serving and the emulators tested together in CI, so that wiring bugs are caught before release.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] TF Serving, Pub/Sub and BigQuery containers started by the tests

issues.title: Drift and fairness monitoring with alerts
issues.body:
As a model owner, I want PSI per input and AIR on live decisions exported as metrics with alert rules, so that I hear about drift before the quarterly review.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Prometheus rules with promtool unit tests
- [ ] Grafana dashboard provisioned
- [ ] replaying 2025 applications against the 2023 reference raises the drift alert

issues.title: One command to run the whole stack
issues.body:
As a reviewer, I want `make up` to start TF Serving, the API, the emulators, the sink, the monitor, Prometheus and Grafana, so that I can try the system in minutes.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] health checks on every service
- [ ] smoke test in CI

issues.title: Load test the decision API
issues.body:
As an engineer, I want k6 results at fixed request rates, so that the latency SLO is backed by a run.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] p50/p95/p99 and error rate committed per rate

issues.title: Terraform for GCP (Cloud Run, Pub/Sub, BigQuery, GCS)
issues.body:
As a platform engineer, I want the cloud deployment as code with least-privilege service accounts and keyless CI deploys, so that it can be recreated from scratch.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] fmt, validate and an IaC security scan pass in CI
- [ ] nothing applied without an account

issues.title: Databricks Asset Bundle for the pipeline
issues.body:
As a data engineer, I want the same Spark jobs defined as a Databricks job on serverless compute, so that the pipeline moves to Databricks without code changes.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] bundle validated against the Databricks bundle JSON schema in CI
- [ ] code runs unchanged on a Databricks session

issues.title: README, architecture diagram and ADRs
issues.body:
As a hiring manager, I want the problem, design, results and limits on one page, so that I can judge the work in two minutes.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] every number links to a committed result file

issues.title: Security: dependency audit, image and IaC scanning
issues.body:
As a security reviewer, I want dependency, secret and IaC scans in CI, so that known issues block a merge.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] pip-audit, gitleaks and trivy config in CI

issues.title: Less discriminatory alternative: joint search with fairness constraints or reweighting
issues.body:
As a compliance officer, I want a model whose adverse impact ratios are at least the lenders' own for every group, at a known cost in AUC, so that a model can be approved.

Sprint 2 found that dropping single inputs cannot fix the age and race gaps together (`reports/ablation.json`, model card). Next: reweighting, monotonic constraints, or a fairness-penalised loss, compared on AUC and AIR at the same operating rule.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] every group's model AIR >= the lenders' observed AIR on 2025, or the trade-off curve that shows it is not reachable
- [ ] chosen variant passes the audit in the model card

issues.title: Less discriminatory alternative, round 2: the parity rule, the advantaged groups and the cost
issues.body:
As a compliance officer, I want an alternative to v1 that passes the whole audit at a cost the business accepts, so that a model can be approved.

Sprint 5 (#27, `reports/lda-search.json`, model card): the referral-rate penalty (lambda 1) passed on 2024 and on 2025 passes all five groups v1 fails, but flags Asian applicants (AIR 1.002 vs the lenders' 1.036) and costs 0.025 AUC and 40.5% referrals instead of 32.7%.

- **The audit rule at parity** (a decision for the audit's owner, before any model change): the rule flags a model AIR more than 0.02 below the lenders' own even when the group is at or above parity with its reference, and equalized odds moves such groups toward parity by construction. Decide whether the rule applies there and record it in an ADR.
- **Constrain the advantaged groups too**: add Asian applicants (and any group above parity) to the referral-rate penalty, or use constrained optimisation with full-data rate estimates (e.g. TensorFlow Constrained Optimization), which would also let the smallest groups (Pacific Islander, about 8 rows a batch) be constrained.
- **The cost**: 24% more referrals for about the same share of denials caught has to fit underwriting capacity.
- **The hold-out**: 2025 has been looked at once for this search. A second variant scored on it is a second look; the card has to say so, or the next choice waits for the 2026 snapshot.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] the audit owner's decision on the parity rule is recorded
- [ ] the chosen variant passes the audit as it then stands, with its AUC and referral-rate cost in the model card
